title: Streamline fetch multiplexer and segment cache lanes to reduce GraphQL tail latency
creator: Liang Chen
description:
Problem: Console GraphQL endpoints occasionally incur long p99 tail latency (400-600ms) under bursty dashboard loads. Root cause analysis points to the fetch multiplexer doing broad fanout and single-heap cache contention during aggregation reads, plus large memoization entries that block the event loop for costly serialization.

Goal: Rework the request fetch multiplexer and introduce segmented cache lanes (route-scoped small caches + a read-through shared tier) to reduce tail latency without regressing throughput or hit-rate economically. This ticket covers design, implementation, canary rollout, and initial observability for the change.

Scope:
- Introduce a light-weight "fetch multiplexer v2" that: groups read requests by route+payload-hash, limits synchronous fanout, and exposes async prefetch hooks.
- Add per-route cache lanes for short-lived hot keys (dashboard cards, token-level cost summaries) with independent TTLs and eviction policies.
- Retain a shared backing cache for larger, cold entries to preserve hit-rate and avoid duplication.
- Instrument end-to-end timing (parse -> resolver -> fetch -> aggregate -> serialize) and add lane-level hit/miss counters to Grafana dashboards.
- Run loadbench + synthetic dashboard trace replay to quantify impact.

Success metrics:
- Reduce GraphQL endpoint p99 latency by >=40% on synthetic dashboard load (baseline: ~480ms p99).
- Keep average token/CPU cost within 10% of baseline at 95th percentile traffic.
- Preserve overall cache hit-rate within 5% of baseline after rollout.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Single global cache vs segmented lanes: chosen segmented lanes to reduce lock contention and provide per-route TTL tuning; cost is slightly higher memory usage and more complex invalidation logic.
- Synchronous coalescing vs async prefetch: implemented bounded sync coalescing for hot keys and async prefetch for known card sequences to avoid request blocking.
- Complexity vs observability: added lane-level metrics and tracing to help compensate for operational complexity.

Related docs and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Console+fetch+multiplexer+v2 (internal)
- Perf playbook and runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Console+perf+playbook
- Benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/main/tools/benchmarks/console-fetch-replay

Notes for reviewers: please focus on the eviction semantics in cache_lane.go and the gating logic in multiplexer/coalesce.go. The implementation uses a per-lane token-bucket to bound bursts; we should validate sizing with infra before wide rollout.
acceptance_criteria: p99 GraphQL latency reduced by >=40% on benchmark suite
Lane-level metrics published to Grafana (explorer: console.fetch.lane.*)
Canary rollout in us-west-2 with no errors or elevated 5xxs for 48h
Unit and integration tests for multiplexer coalescing logic and cache invalidation
